title: {{NAME}} and the Robot That Played Fair
moral: A machine is only as good as the values it was built with.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a high-tech silver and red soccer hero jersey, dark red shorts, and silver-red cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had built FAIR specifically to be the most ethical referee in football history.

Every decision FAIR made was logged, explained, and reviewable. Its judgment system was built on three thousand pages of football rules, precedent, and ethics guidelines.

FAIR's first season as official referee for the Hero Football League: zero disputed decisions.

Not because everyone agreed with FAIR. Because FAIR was always right and always explained why.

"I hate this robot," said the hero who had scored the seventeen goals the previous season.

"You hate that it can't be argued with," said {{NAME}}.

"Same thing," he said.

pages.content:
The real test came in the semifinals.

{{NAME}}'s team was playing. FAIR was refereeing.

In the 78th minute, with the score level, {{NAME}}'s teammate scored what appeared to be the winning goal.

FAIR disallowed it. The ball had crossed the line by centimetres but FAIR's sensor had detected the crossbar contact first, a fraction too late.

{{NAME}}'s team protested. {{NAME}} did not.

He had built FAIR to be exactly this. To be right when it was hardest for him personally.

"It's correct," he told his team. "Play on."

pages.content:
His team lost in extra time.

Afterward, Princess Mira, the league commissioner, came to him.

"You built a referee that cost you the match."

"I built a referee that made the right call," said {{NAME}}.

"Are you glad you built it?"

He thought about it honestly.

"Yes," he said. "If I'd built it to favour my team, it would have been the worst thing I ever made. A referee that's only fair until it costs you something isn't fair at all."

She was quiet.

"You're going to be fine," she said.

pages.content:
FAIR refereed the next four seasons.

In year three, it made a decision that cost the favourite team the championship. The stadium was furious.

The decision was correct. FAIR logged every sensor reading and the league reviewed them and confirmed it.

The furious stadium gradually accepted it.

In year four, the same team benefited from a FAIR decision that was also correct and also tight.

The stadium cheered.

"Same robot," someone said.

"Same rules," said {{NAME}}. "That's the point."

Year four, the crowd cheering a FAIR decision that benefits the previously furious team, {{NAME}} watching with satisfaction, consistency proven. No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
He sat in the empty stadium one evening after a match, FAIR in shutdown mode beside him.

Four seasons. Three thousand decisions. Zero successfully disputed.

He put his hand on FAIR's chassis.

"Good work," he said.

FAIR's status light blinked green, which was its running diagnostic.

But in the quiet of the empty stadium, it felt like something more.

He walked home through the night, satisfied with what he'd built and proud of what it had cost him.

Both things at once.
